newsitem.title: LEBANON: Five Lebanese firms win telephone grid expansion.
newsitem.headline: Five Lebanese firms win telephone grid expansion.

text.p: Five Lebanese telecommunications companies have won bids to install 250,000 new telephone lines for $105 million, an official of the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications said on Thursday.
Ghassan Assi, the ministry's director general of equipment and construction, told Reuters the cabinet on Wednesday awarded the five bids out of 11 submitted by local firms.
The 18-month project is part of an $800-$900 million plan to install 1.7 million lines in Lebanon.

Assi said the five firms were: Muawwad and Edde, al-Zakhem Contracting Company, The Arab Company for Civil Works, The Arab Construction Company and the Modern Roads Company. The bids varied between $15.9 million and $22.98 million.

The 1.7 million lines include one million being currently installed by three international firms, 200,000 lines being installed by local firms, the 250,000 lines to be installed by the five firms and 250,000 more to be installed in the future.

Assi said in September that the government has decided to exclude international firms from the tenders for the 500,000 new lines after the three foreign contractors already working on the telephone grid submitted excessively high bids.

France's Alcatel, Germany's Siemens and Sweden's Ericsson were awarded the bids for a total of $500 million in 1993 and 1994. Works on the one million lines they are installing is expected to be finished at the end of 1997.

Lebanon's ambitious telecommunications project includes the rehabilitation of the country's war-damaged transmission network, laying down fibre optic links with Syria and Egypt and building two satellite earth stations.
